items.note: The page derives the budget Wm-2N+2L for both networks, L=Ich, the ratios 100/539 and 101/539, and s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b<W_bm in full. The complex count s_c=W_cm-2N+2L_c is stated with a link to Binary phase frames, as the assignment asks. It also explains the striking feature, s_b/W_b=m(1-339/(22587335m)), from Iv=3N and Ic_b=N/539.

It writes the form as x.y-(1/9)(x.1)(y.1), finds its eigenvalues 1 and -91/9, and gets <t_S,t_S'>=|S∩S'|-1 from 'dot product |S∩S'| and entry sums 3' (|S∩S'| mod 2 over F_2). The norms {2,1} make the lines nondegenerate, and the neighbour definitions (one shared element for bit, zero or two for complex) give orthogonality. This matches the paper.
It computes the sources explicitly: N lines U_a. For the sinks it computes 'Nm+N(m-1)+(W-2N)m=Wm-N' from the terminal table.
'A wire enters and leaves each gate with that gate's label, so its signed changes telescope to sink minus source dimension, summing to Wm-2N'. This is the paper's telescoping at gates.

It sets up A, P, B, Q and the [G|E] notation, splits A' into four orthogonal pieces to get B'=P'^⊥=(B⊗F)⊥(P⊗t^⊥), and matches the outgoing labels to the next stage's incoming ones. It checks both ends: U_a and 0 at stage 1; F and U_a^⊥ at stage 3 because P'=U_a.

dropped: the physical gate order (Y-side, Y-centre, X-side, X-centre, Y-centre, Y-side, X-centre, X-side) holds at every stage, including stage 2, which runs the inverse schedule with the logical banks exchanged
items.note: With [G|E] encoding A⊗F=(B⊗F)⊥(P⊗F), the centre row [F|F]_3→[F|0]_4 'drops P⊗F⊗Q of dimension h', and all other arrows are inclusions. The page takes from the table which physical wires each time touches and never mentions the stage-2 inversion.

dropped: the per-edge orthogonal residuals and their dimensions (paper's table, e.g. side 0→2 of dimension (a-1)(h-1)+1, scratch last→sink of dimension ah(f-1))
the binary-label part of the lemma: every nonzero residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating, so it has an orthonormal basis (S1.3.6.13-14)
items.note: The label schedule for centre, side, X and Y wires is correct. The page checks that every arrow is an inclusion except centre 3→4, and uses t_X⊥t_Y for side 2→5. It then derives L_b=Ic_bh and L_c=Ic_ch, with nondegeneracy 'like their pieces'. It omits the residual table and the orthonormal-basis claim for binary residuals, which the lemma includes.
'L_b/N=3c_bh/v=30000/161700=100/539' and L_c/N=101/539, from I=3v^2 and N=v^3. Both are correct and below 1/2.

It proves that Π_{U'}-Π_U projects onto U'∩U^⊥, so its rank is the dimension change. It names the exception, the first X_a edge, whose matrix is 2Π_{U_a} with rank one at zero change because B=0 at stage 1. This gives s_b=(W_bm-2N+2L_b)+N. It checks the endpoint identity Π_{U_a^⊥}+Π_{U_a}=Id on X_a→Y_a and Π_F-0 elsewhere, and quotes the numeric value. Faithful to the paper.

dropped: the phase frames C_U and the factorization of each edge difference into one translation kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal basis vector of the residual
